title: How many squares and holes does the carpet have at each step?
description: A square is broken into nine equal squares and the central one is removed, then every square left is treated the same way. The video counts the squares and the holes at Steps zero, one and two. Keeko's doubt is that the count of squares only grows by adding eight each step.
teaching_notes: One idea: every remaining square keeps eight of its nine parts, so the squares multiply by eight, and each remaining square adds one new hole to the old ones. Watch for students who add eight instead of multiplying, or who forget the old hole.

source: Draw Steps 0, 1 and 2 of the Ruhee Carpet and count the
video_script.why: The child knows the carpet rule but has not yet counted what is left after two rounds.
video_script.substitution: Apply the carpet rule to every remaining square, multiply the squares by eight, and add the new holes to the old ones.
video_script.anchor: the Ruhee Carpet of the book, drawn in three frames for Step 0, Step 1 and Step 2
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko adds eight more squares to the eight of Step 1 and says sixteen squares remain. Each of the eight squares becomes eight smaller squares, so the count is multiplied by eight.
video_script.payoff_line: Step two has sixty four squares and nine holes

final_answer.spoken: sixty four squares and nine holes

names.Ruhee: Polish mathematician who discovered the carpet and the triangle

maths_rules: Step 1: a square cut into 3 by 3 gives 9 small squares; remove the centre; 9 - 1 = 8 squares
rule from the book: R(n+1) = 8 x R(n)
rule from the book: H(n+1) = H(n) + R(n)
video_script.design: One carpet in three frames. Every frame stays on the stage and the counts are written under it as they arrive.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; the Ruhee Carpet name; three empty frames labelled Step 0, Step 1 and Step 2

marks.book: the title card and the carpet name appear

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about the carpet that Ruhee discovered.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>We draw the first three steps. Then we count the squares that remain and the holes.
How many squares remain, and how many holes appear, at Step two?

beats.on_screen: the three frames stay on the board with an accent underline

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: one shaded square in the Step 0 frame; the square in the Step 1 frame is cut into a 3 by 3 grid and the central square is removed

marks.rule: one whole shaded square appears in the Step 0 frame
marks.nine: the square in the Step 1 frame is cut into three rows of three equal squares
marks.centre: the central square fades out and leaves a gap

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>The carpet grows by one rule, repeated again and again.
<bookmark mark='nine'/>Break a square into nine equal squares, three rows of three.
<bookmark mark='centre'/>Remove the central one. The gap it leaves is a hole.

beats.on_screen: Given: Step 0 is one square. At each step every remaining square is cut into 9 equal squares and the central one is removed.

marks.given: the starting square and the rule are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, Step zero is one square. Every remaining square is cut into nine, and its central square is removed.

beats.on_screen: To find: remaining squares and holes at Step 0, Step 1 and Step 2

marks.find: the words remaining squares and holes are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the remaining squares and the holes at each of the three steps.

beats.on_screen: Step 0: 1 square, 0 holes. Step 1: 9 - 1 = 8 squares, 1 hole

marks.zero: the counts 1 square and 0 holes are written under the Step 0 frame
marks.one: the line 9 - 1 = 8 squares and 1 hole is written under the Step 1 frame

narration: <bookmark mark='zero'/>Step one, count the first two steps. Step zero has one square and no hole.
<bookmark mark='one'/>Step one has nine small squares, and one is removed. Nine take away one leaves eight squares and one hole.

beats.on_screen: Step 2 squares: each of the 8 squares gives 8, so 8 x 8 = 64

marks.cut: each of the eight squares in the Step 2 frame gets its own grid and loses its centre

narration: <bookmark mark='cut'/>Step two, count the squares. Each of the eight squares is cut into nine and loses its centre, so it gives eight squares.
<bookmark mark='mul'/>Multiply eight squares by eight. Eight times eight is sixty four.

beats.on_screen: Step 2 holes: old holes stay, each of the 8 squares adds 1 new hole, so 1 + 8 = 9

marks.new: the eight new holes flash and the line 1 + 8 = 9 is written

narration: <bookmark mark='old'/>Step three, count the holes. The old hole stays, because a hole is never filled again.
<bookmark mark='new'/>Each of the eight squares adds one new hole. One old hole plus eight new holes is nine holes.

marks.list: the counts 1, 8, 64 and 0, 1, 9 appear under the three frames

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Step two has sixty four squares and nine holes.
<bookmark mark='list'/>The squares go one, eight, sixty four, and the holes go zero, one, nine.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the three frames
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble shows 8 + 8 = 16 squares, struck through; one square of Step 1 is enlarged and cut into its own grid

marks.zoom: one square of Step 1 is enlarged and cut into its own grid
marks.fix: the bubble is struck through and the line 8 x 8 = 64 returns

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks sixteen squares remain, after adding eight more to the eight of Step one.
<bookmark mark='zoom'/>Look at one square of Step one. It is cut again into nine, and eight remain.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>Every square becomes eight squares, so we multiply by eight, and we never add eight.
